title: Rabbi Yeshevav, an Amora
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Yuchasin says that he spoke in Rabbi Levi’s name. Seder HaDorot writes: “I have not found it.”

Hyman indeed finds him named in Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, on “Ulekachtem,” in Baal HaMaor at the end of Rosh Hashanah, and in the Gra’s commentary on Orach Chayim, siman 581, subcomment 25: “Rabbi Yeshevav and Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin in Rabbi Levi’s name: a parable of a province,” etc. But, Hyman argues, Buber’s Pesikta de-Rav Kahana and Kohelet Rabbah, chapter 9, on “Go, eat,” correctly have Rabbi Mani of Shaav; the letters of “from Shaav” became corrupted into Rabbi Yeshevav.

notes.text: The Gra locator means siman 581, subcomment 25. Hyman derives Yeshevav from a corruption of “from Shaav,” retaining Mani of Shaav as the proposed correct reading.

The consulted Kohelet Rabbah 9:7 names Rabbi Mona of Shaav and Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin in Rabbi Levi’s name in the province parable. Hyman’s Mani spelling and proposed Yeshevav corruption are retained. His exact Buber Pesikta, Baal HaMaor, Gra, Yuchasin and Seder HaDorot readings remain attributed reports.
